title: Dynamic PM2.5 Exposure Assessment in Mendoza Metropolitan Area
text: Human exposure air pollution commonly estimated assuming individual remains fixed location throughout day, typically place residence. Although approach simple implement, account daily mobility, activity locations, transportation modes, temporal variations pollutant concentrations. reality, exposure influenced people travel, long remain different locations, characteristics routes use, changes air pollution levels throughout day. result, fixed-location approaches may overestimate underestimate actual personal exposure. AirExposure package implements Dynamic Exposure Method (DEM) integrates mobility patterns, activity schedules, travel routes, hourly pollutant concentration grids estimate daily exposure air pollution. comparison purposes, package also includes Fixed-Location-Based Method (FLBM), assumes individual remains single location entire day. vignette presents complete workflow using hourly PM2.5 concentration grids Mendoza Metropolitan Area (Argentina). objective demonstrate daily mobility can incorporated exposure assessment results compare obtained traditional fixed-location approach. workflow includes: retrieving hourly pollutant concentration grids; estimating exposure using fixed-location approach (FLBM); evaluating alternative travel routes; estimating exposure using mobility-based approach (DEM); comparing results obtained methodologies.

title: Dynamic PM2.5 Exposure Assessment in Mendoza Metropolitan Area
text: case study focuses Mendoza Metropolitan Area, located western Argentina. Mendoza one country’s largest urban agglomerations experiences substantial spatial temporal variability air pollutant concentrations associated traffic, urban activities, meteorological conditions. Hourly PM2.5 concentration fields used represent spatial temporal variability air pollution across study area. example presented vignette corresponds 1 August 2019, separate pollutant grid available hour day. use hourly pollutant grids allows exposure estimates account changes PM2.5 concentrations throughout day across different locations within metropolitan area. methodology implemented AirExposure Mendoza case study described publications listed References section.

title: Dynamic PM2.5 Exposure Assessment in Mendoza Metropolitan Area
text: Traditional exposure assessment methods commonly assume individual remains single location throughout day, typically place residence. approach referred Fixed-Location-Based Method (FLBM). AirExposure, FLBM implemented traditional_model() function. method estimates exposure identifying grid cell containing origin location, calculating average pollutant concentration entire day, assuming continuous exposure location 24-hour period. following example estimates daily exposure residential location Mendoza Metropolitan Area. Although approach widely used due simplicity, consider daily mobility, activity locations, route choice, temporal changes pollutant concentrations associated travel. Dynamic Exposure Method (DEM), presented following sections, addresses limitations explicitly incorporating individual mobility patterns exposure assessment process.
code: home_location <- data.frame(   longitude = -68.8320,   latitude = -32.9058 )  traditional_exposure <- traditional_model(   origin_point = home_location,   date = "2019-08-01",   dir = grid_dir,   gridID = "ID",   shapeValue = "value" )

title: Dynamic PM2.5 Exposure Assessment in Mendoza Metropolitan Area
text: Alternative routes may differ travel duration, distance, traffic conditions, pollutant concentrations. AirExposure uses TomTom Routing API retrieve alternative routes origin destination combines routes hourly pollutant concentration grids. alternative_trajectories() function compares available routes according several criteria, including: shortest route; fastest route; least polluted route; polluted route; lowest exposure route; highest exposure route. example illustrates alternative routes can evaluated using Mendoza PM2.5 dataset. resulting object contains route-level summaries, including travel time, distance, average pollutant concentration, estimated exposure. Route comparison particularly important route lowest pollutant concentration necessarily route associated lowest exposure. Exposure depends concentration levels travel duration. route-level assessment provides basis Dynamic Exposure Method (DEM) implemented AirExposure used following sections.
code: routes <- alternative_trajectories(   origin = "-32.9058,-68.8320",   dest = "-32.8705,-68.8320",   mode = "car",   hours = "2019-08-01 08:00:00",   key = "YOUR_API_KEY",   dir = grid_dir,   gridID = "ID",   shapeValue = "value",   pollutant = "PM2.5",   units = "ug/m3",   output = "df" )

title: Dynamic PM2.5 Exposure Assessment in Mendoza Metropolitan Area
text: Dynamic Exposure Method (DEM) extends traditional exposure assessment incorporating daily mobility patterns, travel routes, activity schedules, hourly pollutant concentrations. AirExposure, DEM implemented total_exposure() function. method integrates: origin destination locations; travel routes obtained TomTom Routing API; travel modes; activity durations; hourly pollutant concentration grids; route selection criteria. example represents simplified daily schedule consisting trip home activity location, period spent location, return trip. resulting object contains estimates exposure accumulated travel, exposure associated activities destination locations, total daily exposure. accounting mobility temporal changes air pollution, DEM provides realistic representation individual exposure fixed-location approaches.
code: travel_list <- data.frame(   long = c(-68.8320, -68.8320),   lat = c(-32.9058, -32.8705) )  activity_minutes <- data.frame(   minutes = 300 )  daily_exposure <- total_exposure(   travel_list = travel_list,   mode = c("car", "car"),   dir = grid_dir,   key = "YOUR_API_KEY",   selection = c("fast", "fast"),   output_exp = "df",   departure_time_home = "2019-08-01 08:00:00",   activity_minutes = activity_minutes,   pollutant = "PM2.5",   shapeValue = "value",   gridID = "ID",   units = "ug/m3" )
